editorial:
Imagine if Superman's pod landed in the Soviet Union instead of a farm in Kansas. That is the wild setup here. You get to see a version of Clark Kent who grows up as a champion for communism and Stalin instead of the American way. It turns the whole hero story on its head and makes you wonder if he would still be a good guy if he had a different boss. The vibe is tense and political, but it still feels like a classic superhero story with huge stakes and cool powers.

The voice acting is great and keeps the story moving quickly, though some of the animation can feel a bit stiff in a few spots. You will love the twists and the way it handles the rivalry between the US and USSR. If you enjoy a good 'what if' story, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: After a huge fight, Superman realizes that his attempt to create a perfect world through force is actually a mistake. He sees that people need freedom to truly be happy. In a surprising twist, he decides to leave Earth entirely. He lets the world heal on its own without a super-powered dictator. He departs for space, leaving humanity to find its own path and live in peace without his control.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves comic books and alternate history stories.
